note: Lean defines the two-form metric directly and proves its reduced one-form as a Schur complement (`rotor_law`) with the Lagrange-type matrix identity `blade_price`; the minimum over phi with weights w_a is never stated, so the closed form is reached as a different quantity.

snippet.text:
lemma rotor_law : rotor S k v p=fieldI S k v p -
    (scaleR S k v p)⁻¹ • (fieldI S k v p * signal S 0 p * mirage S 0 p * fieldI S k v p) := by
  let a := scaleR S k v p; have ha : a≠0 := scaleR_live S k hk v hp he

proof_context.conclusion: `rotor` (mirage * pulse * signal, the one-form quadratic form of the two-form metric) equals `fieldI` minus `(scaleR)⁻¹ fieldI signal mirage fieldI`, the Schur complement of the diagonal precision after eliminating the gradient.

snippet.text:
lemma blade_price (x y t : Axis → ℂ) :
    (wedge 1 x).transpose*mask 2 t*wedge 1 y=(∑ i, x i*(t i*y i)) • mask 1 t -
      mask 1 t * wedge 0 y * (wedge 0 x).transpose * mask 1 t := by
  rw [Matrix.mul_assoc,mask_insert,← Matrix.mul_assoc,crossed, sub_mul, smul_mul_assoc, one_mul,
    mask_insert,mask_nil,Matrix.mul_one]

proof_context.conclusion: The matrix identity (wedge 1 x)^T mask 2 t (wedge 1 y) = (sum x t y) mask 1 t - mask 1 t (wedge 0 y)(wedge 0 x)^T mask 1 t, the Lagrange identity behind the closed form.
